commandPowerShell: docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --user 65534:65534 --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,nodev,size=1m,mode=0700,uid=65534,gid=65534 --mount "type=bind,source=$((Get-Location).Path)\spikes\tls,target=/proof,readonly" cafi-spikes:s1 python /proof/proof.py
binding: CPython stdlib ctypes, direct SSL_connect and SSL_accept on TCP sockets
transport: Fresh TCP sockets on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral listening port for each case; each positive case requires a one-byte acknowledgment over TLS after both peers are authenticated.
certificateFixtures: Two independent local CAs and role-specific P-256/SHA-256 server/client leaves. Both trust only lab-ca. The untrusted leaves keep the expected SAN but chain to the other CA. Wrong server name matches the legitimate leaf's CN, not its SAN. Wrong client identity has a valid lab-ca chain and expected CN but a different SAN.

observation.group: SSL_get0_group_name on each successfully handshaken SSL object; NULL fails. Literal result is x25519, compared case-insensitively to the pinned X25519.
observation.peerValidation: SSL_VERIFY_PEER on both roles, SSL_VERIFY_FAIL_IF_NO_PEER_CERT on the server, SSL_set1_host with no wildcards or subject fallback. SSL_get0_peername, SSL_get_verify_result, SSL_get0_peer_certificate and SSL_get0_verified_chain on each peer.
observation.certificateAlgorithm: X509_get0_pubkey, EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name, EVP_PKEY_get_group_name and X509_get_signature_nid / OBJ_nid2sn. prime256v1 denotes P-256.
observation.session: SSL_session_reused, SSL_SESSION_has_ticket, SSL_SESSION_is_resumable and SSL_get_early_data_status, checked before and after acknowledgment; second connection reuses both SSL_CTX objects, not sockets or SSL objects.
observation.rejection: SSL_get_error, OpenSSL error queue, and SSL_get_verify_result. A local SSL_connect return of 1 in a client-certificate rejection is not acceptance: the server failed SSL_accept and the client received a fatal TLS alert on read.

clientHandshake.verifyReason: unable to get local issuer certificate

serverHandshake.verifyReason: unable to get local issuer certificate

serverHandshake.reason: peer did not return a certificate

failurePropagation.observed: The designated positive TLS handshake was rejected (hostname mismatch, X.509 code 62); the proof raised RuntimeError without printing success JSON.

missingDependency.command: Same Docker options and image; replace the entrypoint arguments after the image with: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/proof'); import proof; proof.LIBSSL = proof.LIBSSL.with_name('missing-libssl.so.3'); proof.run()"
missingDependency.observed: ctypes.CDLL raised OSError for the nonexistent libssl; no fallback or success JSON.

limitations: OpenSSL CLI used only to issue certificates in the restricted tmpfs; no keys, certificates, payload bytes, or TLS secrets are retained in evidence. No connection uses message-signing keys.
Isolated same-process, same-implementation proof. No active PSK/0-RTT injection, external interoperability, revocation, application authorization, financial connectors, or production stack approval.
No hybrid handshake or hybrid incompatibility case was run in S1-06.
